## Image 6 Log-Concavity Image

A large number of naturally-occurring combinatorial sequences exhibit the logarithmically concave (log-concave) property [31]. Further to saturation, experimental data that we have looked-at so far has shown that coefficients of the Markov polynomials are log-concave in all directions.

###### Definition 6.1. Image

A sequence x=({x}_{0},{x}_{1},\mathrm{\dots },{x}_{n}) is said to be log-concave if it satisfies the property

(25)  |  | {x}_{k}^{2}\ge {x}_{k-1}{x}_{k+1},  | 

for k\in \{1,2,\mathrm{\dots },n-1\}.

A well-known example is the binomial sequence {x}_{k}=\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{k}\right),k=0,\mathrm{\dots },n:

 | \frac{{x}_{k}^{2}}{{x}_{k-1}{x}_{k+1}}={\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{k}\right)}^{2}/\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{k-1}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{k+1}\right)=\frac{k+1}{k}\frac{n-k+1}{n-k}>1.  | 

###### Definition 6.2. Image

We say that the weights on the Newton polygon satisfy the weak log-concavity property if their sequences in all principal directions (horizontal, vertical and diagonal with i+j=\text{constant}) are log-concave.

###### Conjecture 6.3. Image

(Log-concavity conjecture) The coefficients of Markov polynomials are weakly log-concave on the corresponding Newton polygon.

Note that the Conjecture 6.3 implies the Saturation Conjecture 3.3, claiming the positivity of all the coefficients inside the Newton polygon. Indeed, we know that the coefficients on the boundary are positive, so the appearance of internal zero coefficients will contradict the log-concavity property (25).

###### Theorem 6.4. Image

Conjecture 6.3 holds for the Markov-Fibonacci polynomials.

###### Proof.

We need to check the log-concavity condition in all three principal directions. Using (16), in the horizontal direction we have

 | {A}_{i,j}^{2}={\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n-j}{n+1-i-j}\right)}^{2}{\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{i+j}{j}\right)}^{2}=\left(\frac{{(n-j)!}^{2}}{{(n+1-i-j)!}^{2}{(i-1)!}^{2}}\right)\left(\frac{{(i+j)!}^{2}}{{i!}^{2}{j!}^{2}}\right),  | 
 | {A}_{i-1,j}{A}_{i+1,j}  | =\left({\displaystyle \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n-j}{n+2-i-j}}\right)\left({\displaystyle \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n-j}{n-i-j}}\right)\left({\displaystyle \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{i+j-1}{j}}\right)\left({\displaystyle \genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{i+j+1}{j}}\right)  | 

with both of the final fractions being greater than 1 (the first requires that i\ge 1 but the vertical line for i=0 consists of only a single point, so can be ignored).

In the diagonal case the second binomials in {A}_{i-1,j+1},{A}_{i,j},{A}_{i+1,j-1} are respectively \left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{i+j}{j+1}\right),\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{i+j}{j}\right),\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{i+j}{j-1}\right), which are consecutive binomial coefficients satisfying the log-concavity property. As a result we have

 | \frac{{A}_{i,j}^{2}}{{A}_{i-1,j+1}{A}_{i+1,j-1}}\ge \left(\frac{{(n-j)!}^{2}}{(n-j+1)!(n-j-1)!}\right)\left(\frac{(n-i-j)!(n+2-i-j)!}{{(n+1-i-j)!}^{2}}\right)  | 
 | =\left(\frac{n-j}{n-j+1}\right)\left(\frac{n+2-i-j}{n+1-i-j}\right)=\frac{(n-j)(n+1-i-j)+(n-j)}{(n-j)(n+1-i-j)+(n+1-i-j)},  | 

which is greater than or equal to 1 as required. ∎

The Conjecture 6.3 holds along the boundaries of the polygon, since these coefficients are precisely binomial coefficients, which are known to be log-concave. We will show now that this holds also on the 2nd horizontal line and upper diagonal of the Newton polygon.

###### Lemma 6.5. Image

Sequences of the form

 | {x}_{k}=A\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right)+B\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right),k=0,1,\mathrm{\dots },c  | 

for positive A,B,c are always log-concave.

###### Proof.

We have

 | {x}_{k}^{2}={A}^{2}{\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right)}^{2}+2AB\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right)+{B}^{2}{\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right)}^{2},  | 
 | \begin{array}{c}{x}_{k-1}{x}_{k+1}={A}^{2}\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k+1}\right)+AB\left[\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right)+\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-2}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k+1}\right)\right]\hfill \\ \hfill +{B}^{2}\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-2}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right).\end{array}  | 

It is clear that the coefficients of {A}^{2} and {B}^{2} are greater in the case of {x}_{k}^{2} due to the log-concavity of the binomial coefficients. So if we can show that

 | \left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right)\ge \left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-2}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k+1}\right),  | 

then the result will follow. Since

 | \frac{\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-1}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k}\right)}{\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k-2}\right)\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{c}{k+1}\right)}=\frac{k+1}{k-1}\frac{c-k+2}{c-k}>1,  | 

this completes the proof. ∎

###### Theorem 6.6. Image

The coefficients of Markov polynomial {M}_{\rho } that appear on the lines with j=1 and i+j=a+b-2 of its Newton polygon are strictly log-concave.

###### Proof.

The proof follows from Theorem 4.2 and the previous lemma. ∎

As for the 3rd diagonal we are only able to prove the log-concavity in the case where \rho \le 3/5.

###### Theorem 6.7. Image

The coefficients of Markov polynomials {M}_{\rho } that appear on the line with i+j=a+b-3 of its Newton polygon are log-concave for \frac{a}{b}\le \frac{3}{5}.

###### Proof.

We will use the following result quoted by Stanley [31] (but which dates back to Newton [25]).

###### Theorem 6.8 (Stanley [31]). Image

Let p(X)={\sum }_{k=0}^{n}{\alpha }_{k}{X}^{k}. If the polynomial p(X) has only real zeros, then the sequence {\alpha }_{k} is log-concave.

Let {\alpha }_{k} be the coefficients on the diagonal i+j-3 stated in Theorem 4.2:

 | {\alpha }_{k}=E\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{a+b-3}{k}\right)+F\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{a+b-4}{k-1}\right)+G\left(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{a+b-5}{k-2}\right),  | 
 | E=\frac{(a-1)(a-2)}{2},F=a(b-a-1),G=\frac{1}{2}\left[{(b-a)}^{2}+5a-3b\right].  | 

Let

 | p(X)=\sum _{k=0}^{a+b-3}{\alpha }_{k}{X}^{k},  | 

then we have

 | p(X)  | =E{(1+X)}^{a+b-3}+FX{(1+X)}^{a+b-4}+G{X}^{2}{(1+X)}^{a+b-5}  | 
 |  | ={(1+X)}^{a+b-5}\left[E{(1+X)}^{2}+FX(1+X)+G{X}^{2}\right]={(1+X)}^{a+b-5}q(X),  | 

where

 | q(X)  | :=(E+F+G){X}^{2}+(2E+F)X+E  | 
 |  | ={\displaystyle \frac{(b-1)(b-2)}{2}}{X}^{2}+(ab-4a+2)X+{\displaystyle \frac{(a-1)(a-2)}{2}}  | 

Since {(1+X)}^{a+b-5} has clearly real roots, to apply Theorem 6.8 we need to show that q(X) has only real roots. The discriminant \mathrm{\Delta } of q(X) is

 | \mathrm{\Delta }  | ={(ab-4a+2)}^{2}-4{\displaystyle \frac{(b-1)(b-2)}{2}}{\displaystyle \frac{(a-1)(a-2)}{2}}  | 
 |  | ={(ab-4a+2)}^{2}-(ab-2a-b+2)(ab-a-2b+2).  | 

If a/b\le 3/5 then a+2b\ge 4a+\frac{a}{3} and 2a+b\ge 4a-\frac{a}{3}, so

 | \mathrm{\Delta }  | \ge {(ab-4a+2)}^{2}-\left(ab-4a+2+{\displaystyle \frac{a}{3}}\right)\left(ab-4a+2-{\displaystyle \frac{a}{3}}\right)={\displaystyle \frac{{a}^{2}}{9}}\ge 0.  | 

∎

# Schur-positivity and log-concavity of anti-Markov polynomials

Prove that, for every anti-Markov number $a\geq 2$, the anti-Markov polynomial $\widetilde{\{a\}}$ is Schur-positive and has a log-concave $(q,t)$)-expansion.

### Background

The paper introduces symmetric $(q,t)$(q,t))-analogues of Markov numbers through a Markov-type equation and defines anti-Markov polynomials by applying the involution that changes the sign of $e_2$e 2​.

The authors state that computed examples suggest $\gamma$γ-anti-positivity for polynomials associated with odd-indexed Pell numbers. They establish Schur-positivity for the ordinary Markov polynomials in one proposition, report that log-concavity was checked computationally through $a\leq135137$a≤135137, and then formulate the unresolved conjecture for anti-Markov polynomials.

This pushes us to make the following conjecture (as we also checked it up to the same bound): \begin{conjecture} For all anti-Markov number $a\geq 2$, the polynomial $#1{a}$ is Schur-positive, and its $(q,t)$-expansion is log-concave. \end{conjecture}
